checks.upstream_cause: e5c7cde5c812 '[NFC][TableGen] Refactor getIntrinsicFnAttributeSet (#106587)' is an ancestor of llvmorg-20.1.8 and not of llvmorg-19.1.7. Its diff replaces the llvmorg-19.1.7 gate '(Int.ME != MemoryEffects::unknown() && !Int.hasSideEffects) || !canThrow || ...' in Intrinsic::getAttributes with hasFnAttributes(Int), which tests getEffectiveME(Int) != unknown. getEffectiveME only widens readnone+side-effects to unknown. As a result, IntrReadMem/IntrWriteMem + IntrHasSideEffects + Throws went from no fn attributes to memory(read)/memory(write). This is exactly the drift observed. Checked with opt -S on the two declarations: ref-18 none, port-19 none, integration head (logs/20-F022/base) and build/int-20 give pop memory(read) and push memory(write), build/20-F022 none.
checks.upstream_pattern: int_xcore_in/int_xcore_out (IntrinsicsXCore.td at 20.1.8) have no memory property. That matches the fix and is a reasonable reference for channel/stream intrinsics. Unknown memory is also correct rather than IntrInaccessibleMemOnly, because SSR streams read and write user memory at the configured addresses.

checks.ir_behaviour: F014 reproducer logs/20-F022/frep-indep.c at clang -O2 -march=rv32imafd_xfrep0p1_xssr0p1_xdma0p1: at the integration head all ssr.pop calls sit in entry/for.cond.cleanup blocks and the asm has fdiv.d fa4,ft0,ft1 outside the loops. With 20-F022 every pop pair is inside for.body4*, and the asm has fdiv.d in every inner loop, like ref-18. My own IR cases (pop in loop, pop in loop with store, reduction loop with constant trip count, two pops in a row, dead pop, push then pop, two pushes, push in loop, load across pop, store/push/store) went through default<O2>, default<O3>, early-cse<memssa>, gvn, loop-mssa(licm), dse, instcombine and sink. 20-F022 output is identical to ref-18 for every pass. The only difference is an upstream-20 'initializes' param attribute under O2. Before the fix, EarlyCSE/GVN/O2 merged two_pops into one pop and CSE'd a load across a pop. After the fix neither happens. Dead pops and repeated pushes are kept both before and after, because Throws means no willreturn.

checks.push_change_judgement: Changing push was appropriate. No push miscompile was shown at int-20: my DSE, LICM and O2 cases produce the same output before and after for push, because Throws already blocks the risky transforms. Still, memory(write) is semantically wrong: it claims push reads no state, but a push reads and advances its stream address counter. It is also a change from ref-18/port-19 caused only by the upstream emitter refactor. The change restores the fork's pre-20 attribute model exactly. TableGen then forces the matching mayLoad on the push pseudo, which is byte-neutral.

checks.note: The note has all four sections. It cites the upstream commit with the old and new gate lines and the fork commit that relied on the old behaviour. It names the observable symptom (the stream element is reused across iterations and the stream falls out of step). Rule 12's reference is XCore instead of XCV. That is justified: CORE-V has no stream registers, and the note says so.

non_blocking_observations: IntrinsicsRISCVXsnitch.td keeps the old 'Throws ensures ... LICM' comment and TODO next to the new, more accurate comment. This is harmless, but the old comment is now misleading about what actually protects the calls: the missing memory property does, while Throws only adds a guard against deletion. It can be cleaned up when the stack collapses.

In isolated LICM runs on simple pop loops, int-20 did not hoist the pop either, because the call is not willreturn/nounwind. The hoist in the reproducer appears only in the full -O2 pipeline (after unrolling/rotation). The EarlyCSE/GVN merge of consecutive pops is the direct, minimal miscompile. The proposed regression test in the result file should keep the cse_pop case, not only a LICM case.

As the worker notes, the upstream TODO in getEffectiveME means any future fork intrinsic declared IntrReadMem/IntrWriteMem together with IntrHasSideEffects will again be optimisable. This is worth a checklist item.
